Prioritise a to-do list when everything feels urgent

When every task feels important, sorting the whole list is paralysing. Choosing which of two to do first takes a second each, and a few dozen of those choices give you an order you can start on.

Opens the free ranker with the list below already filled in. Change it there with "Start over", or paste your own list.

The starter list

Question: "Which should I do first?"

  1. Reply to the overdue emails
  2. Finish the quarterly report
  3. Book the dentist
  4. File expense receipts
  5. Prepare for Monday's meeting
  6. Fix the leaking tap
  7. Call the bank about the fee
  8. Update my CV
  9. Plan next week's meals
  10. Clear the inbox
  11. Renew the car insurance
  12. Back up my laptop

Why picking pairs works here

  • Replace the starter tasks with your own; paste a list straight from your notes app, one task per line (bullets are stripped).
  • "Be sure of the favourite" mode spends its questions on the front-runners when you only need to know what to start on.
  • Nothing leaves your browser, so work and personal tasks can share the list.

What it doesn't do: It orders the tasks by what you judge more pressing in each pair; it does not know your deadlines. Put tasks with a fixed date first yourself.

Compared with what you'd use today

An Eisenhower matrix, numbering tasks 1 to 3, or a task app's priority flags. Those ask you to label each task in isolation; comparing two at a time is easier when everything feels like a 1.

Under the hood: a Bradley-Terry model refit after every answer, an adaptive question picker, and a stop rule checked against simulated respondents, including ones whose picks are close calls. The method and its measurements.
